assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis turned a laboratory chemistry (reversible terminator nucleotides, single-molecule and cluster fluorescence readout) into the general tool that underlies genomics, cancer biology and my own field's ability to study replication errors and mutational signatures. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa chemistry is most clearly attributable to Balasubramanian and Klenerman; Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Ju (terminator chemistry) and Mayer (parallel clonal arrays) also contributed, so a clean two or three person split is contestable. I would keep the chemical-core pair.
assessment.maturity: Four-plus decades of independent confirmation and universal adoption; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Competing parallel inventions (454, Solexa, Mayer, Ju) make the allocation of credit disputed.
I have not independently verified the exact invention chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are a chemical solution to genome editing: engineered deaminases convert one base to another on DNA without double-strand breaks. The reaction is a defined chemistry (cytidine and adenosine deamination plus repair manipulation) and gives biologists a general tool with direct therapeutic relevance.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived and led the work; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, including the evolved deaminase) carried the decisive experiments. Liu alone or Liu with the two first authors are both plausible; I choose all three.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many laboratories and already in clinical trials, with first patient benefit emerging. Timing is reasonable though the CRISPR prize (2020) may make the committee cautious about a second genome-editing award; off-target and bystander editing are still being characterised.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may lower appetite.
Long-term clinical safety evidence is still accumulating.
Independent base-editor work by Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) could complicate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology: a bifunctional molecule or a molecular glue hijacks an E3 ligase to destroy a target. The discovery of the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism and the PROTAC concept gave a general chemical strategy for formerly undruggable proteins, with strong biomedical relevance.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (PROTAC concept and first demonstrations) and Handa (cereblon as thalidomide target, a key mechanistic link) are the most decisive; Ciulli, Gray, Ito, Sakamoto and Kim also made important contributions, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials, and many labs reproduced the mechanism, but approvals are still pending, so recognition could be slightly early.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution between PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages.
Whether the committee treats it as one discovery or two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis converts light into controlled single-electron transfer in organic synthesis, broadly used in pharmaceutical and academic chemistry. The mechanism is well-defined and the tool is general.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced synthetic photoredox catalysis in 2008-2011; MacMillan (already a 2021 laureate) and others expanded it. König, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre add precedent and later contributions, so attribution is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, widely reproduced and applied; the main question is whether the 2021 organocatalysis prize makes the committee reluctant.
uncertainties: MacMillan's earlier prize complicates a fair configuration.
Earlier precedent (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, others) weakens priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs reprogrammed the genetic code, giving chemists a general way to place new chemistry into proteins in living cells.
assessment.attribution: Schultz, with Wang, established the first orthogonal pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended to quadruplet codons and genome-recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Reproducible and widely used for two decades, with therapeutic uses (site-specific conjugates) appearing, so timing is fine.
uncertainties: Share between Schultz, Chin and Wang remains debatable.
Overlap with the 2018 evolution prize and 2024 protein design prize might reduce room.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the mutant KRAS G12C cysteine, via the switch-II pocket, showed a supposedly undruggable oncogene could be inhibited and led to approved drugs. Chemical genetics of analogue-sensitive kinases is another general tool.
assessment.attribution: Credit centres on Shokat for both KRAS and chemical genetics; drug development at Amgen and Mirati built on his work, so the clinical translation involves many others.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) confirm the concept, though durability of response and resistance remain open.
uncertainties: Whether the prize rewards the academic discovery versus the industrial drugs.
Resistance in clinical use is not yet resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structure of the FeMo-cofactor and the biochemical mechanism of nitrogenase address one of the most important reactions in biology, N2 reduction, and measure the chemistry of a complex metallocluster. Strong enzymology and bioinorganic interest.
assessment.attribution: Rees and colleagues solved the structures; Einsle provided the high-resolution cofactor with the central carbide; Seefeldt contributed the mechanistic work. Dean and Ribbe are also relevant, so credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding steps are still being refined, which weakens the case for now.
uncertainties: The mechanism of N2 reduction is not fully settled.
Credit is distributed among many structural and biochemical groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A RNA methylation, with writers, erasers and readers, opened epitranscriptomics as a regulatory chemistry layer in RNA, with links to development, cancer and ageing.
assessment.attribution: He identified the demethylase FTO activity and the chemical-biology framework; Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini) provided transcriptome-wide maps in 2012. The allocation among mapping and enzymology contributions is open.
assessment.maturity: Recent and rapidly changing; some mapping methods and quantitative stoichiometry claims have been disputed and require independent confirmation, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Quantitative reliability of mapping methods remains debated.
Biological functions of FTO and some readers are still being clarified.
May be viewed as a medicine or physiology topic.
